title: A Crown for the Wolf
premise: Beatrix Eriksen serves as royal food-taster by day and ledger-keeper for the Guild of Impossible Things by night, a trade in souls, debts, and favors that the crown pretends not to see. When she discovers her own death date written in a century-old prophecy — and learns the prince she's secretly sworn to protect is fated to drag her into it — the two are forced into an uneasy alliance. To cheat the prophecy, they must steal back the soul the crown sold to the court beneath the mountain, the same soul that keeps the long winter falling. In the end, Beatrix must choose between exposing the crown's crime and preserving the fragile loyalty she's built, and she pays the price with her own name, erased from every ledger but one.
about_author: Wren Dunmore is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval debt records and never quite recovered. They write fantasy about people whose jobs are stranger than their magic.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. She tastes the king's supper, catalogues the poisons in her body like old friends, and slips away to the Guild's cellar to balance ledgers of impossible debts. Introduces her double life and her quiet rule: record everything, feel nothing. Beat: competent loneliness.

chapters.title: A Debt Written in Ash
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. Auditing the Guild's oldest ledger, she finds an entry dated tonight — her own name, entered a century ago in a hand that matches hers. The entry lists a debt owed to the court beneath the mountain. Beat: cold dread disguised as curiosity.

chapters.title: The Prince Who Cannot Sleep
chapters.summary: Prince Aldric, POV. Sleepless and hunted by courtiers who want him declared unfit, Aldric visits the Guild to buy something impossible: one honest answer. He and Beatrix collide over the same ledger page. Beat: wary recognition of a fellow prisoner.

chapters.title: Tonight, As Promised
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. The prophecy's date arrives. Aldric is attacked at the winter feast with a poison only Beatrix recognizes — one she tasted once and survived. She saves him publicly, exposing her immunity and making them both suspects. Beat: the trap springs.

chapters.title: The Guild Closes Its Doors
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Oren, POV. The crown moves to seize the Guild's cellars. Oren burns the soft ledgers, keeps the hard one, and gives Beatrix the century-old page, telling her the prophecy is a receipt, not a prediction. Beat: betrayal of the old order, passing of the burden.

chapters.title: What the Mountain Was Promised
chapters.summary: Beatrix and Aldric, alternating. Fleeing the city, they piece together the truth: a hundred years ago the crown sold a soul to the under-court to end a famine, and the long winter is the interest coming due. Beat: the horror of inherited crimes.

chapters.title: The Road That Remembers
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. On the mountain road, the land itself tests them — snow that falls upward, villages where everyone shares one face. Beatrix realizes her immunity is not natural; she was made for this journey. Beat: identity shaken at its foundation.

chapters.title: An Inn with No Keeper
chapters.summary: Aldric, POV. Sheltering at an inn that shouldn't exist, Aldric confesses he has visited the Guild before — to sell a memory of his mother's death, the crown's price for sparing him. Beatrix must decide if loyalty can survive a lie of omission. Beat: trust cracked, not broken.

chapters.title: The Tollgate of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. A border spirit demands payment in truths. Beatrix trades the secret that she has been slowly poisoning herself for years, building immunity as a slow suicide plan. Aldric overhears. Beat: vulnerability as currency.

chapters.title: Descent at the Year's Turning
chapters.summary: Both, alternating. They reach the mountain's mouth as the winter solstice nears and the prophecy's final clause activates: only the taster may enter, and only the prince may call her back. Beat: the point of no return, chosen together.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. The under-court is a mirrored palace where the sold soul — a girl named Ylva, still aware after a century — serves as the winter's living wick. The under-king offers Beatrix a trade: Ylva's freedom for her ledgers, every debt the Guild ever held. Beat: temptation dressed as justice.

chapters.title: Ledger of the Under-King
chapters.summary: Aldric, POV. Aldric bargains with the under-court while Beatrix is held as collateral, learning the crown's current king renewed the debt — his own father — and that the prophecy was written by the first taster, Beatrix's ancestor, who failed. Beat: the weight of the past made personal.

chapters.title: A Taste of Ash and Iron
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. To prove her worth, Beatrix must taste the under-court's feast — dishes brewed from regrets. Each dish strips away a memory she chose to keep. She fights to hold onto the memory of why she started keeping ledgers at all. Beat: identity consumed.

chapters.title: The Escape That Was Expected
chapters.summary: Both, alternating. Their theft of Ylva succeeds too easily; the under-king let them go because the debt requires a taster to return willingly. Beatrix realizes the prophecy needs her consent, not her death. Beat: the trap inside the trap.

chapters.title: What Ylva Remembers of the Sun
chapters.summary: Ylva, POV. On the ascent, Ylva recounts the famine and the crown's choice a century ago — and reveals the soul was sold not by the king but by the Guild, by Oren's predecessor. The Guild's justice is compromised too. Beat: no institution is clean.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Finishes Falling
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. They surface into the prophecy's final night: the winter that will not end, the capital buried, the king demanding Ylva be returned to preserve his bargain. Beatrix must choose the law, the Guild, or the truth. Beat: all loyalties at war.

chapters.title: The Trial of the Taster
chapters.summary: Aldric, POV. In the frozen throne room, the king accuses Beatrix of treason. Aldric, heir apparent, must testify — and instead reads the crown's century of debts aloud from the hard ledger, committing treason himself. Beat: loyalty finally aligned with truth.

chapters.title: A Crown for the Wolf
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. The under-king rises through the palace floors to collect. Beatrix offers the only payment that satisfies: not a soul, but the ledger itself — the record that makes the debt real — plus her consent, freely given, breaking the prophecy's mechanism. Beat: the climax, paid in identity.

chapters.title: One Name Erased
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. The debt dissolves; the winter breaks. But the price is her name, struck from every record, memory, and tongue — even Aldric's. She walks out of the palace a stranger to everyone she saved. Beat: triumph laced with grief.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Keeps the Ledgers
chapters.summary: Ylva, POV. Ylva, freed and mortal, takes up the Guild's hard ledger and writes one new entry: Beatrix Eriksen, debt paid in full. Naming her back into the world, one line at a time. Beat: memory as an act of loyalty.

chapters.title: The Taster's New Tongue
chapters.summary: Aldric, POV. Crowned in a thawing kingdom, Aldric abolishes the taster's office and the debts it served, then seeks out the nameless woman living at the mountain's edge. He cannot remember her, but he cannot stay away. Beat: love outlasting memory.

chapters.title: A Ledger with One Blank Page
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. Beatrix, half-remembering herself through Ylva's written entries, chooses to stay — not as taster, traitor, or keeper, but as the author of a new ledger with one blank page. The last line is her name, written in her own hand. Beat: identity reclaimed by choice, not inheritance.
